expected_per_acceptance: Proactive reconnect during idle; messages arrive in causal order. (BA spec lines 162-170)
gap_analysis: Could not reproduce disconnect within timeboxed run. Concrete obstacles encountered: (1) Spawning a new clean session in /tmp/dev-verify-131502-510 was attempted via 'Start New Session' button, but clicking the path-selector field on the new-session form bounced the browser back to the existing seed session (route changed from /new to /session/<existing-id>) — the path selector did not open an editable text input, suggesting it is a fixed picker/dropdown. (2) Even if path selection succeeded, the BA-spec acceptance scenario requires sending a long-running task and waiting >2 minutes for the WebSocket idle threshold to be exceeded, plus additional time to send '2+2' and observe message ordering — total ~5-10 minutes per BA spec line 257-260 — well beyond the 8-minute timebox imposed on this re-run after rate-limit. (3) No prior partial JSON existed from the prior agent (per orchestrator note: '1 initial screenshot + network log but no JSON'), so no measurements could be inherited. (4) WebSocket frame timestamps are not exposed by mcp__playwright__browser_network_requests (it returns only HTTP REST entries), making direct WS-disconnect/reconnect observation harder than DevTools Network panel would allow. The BA spec at line 263 explicitly authorizes 'BLOCKED — could not reproduce disconnect within timeboxed run' as the correct verdict for this fragile scenario, and Section 7 of the spec already lists §5.10 as carry-forward for a dedicated cycle.
